description: CSMIC laboratory, PANalytical Empyrean, Cu LFF tube, parallel-beam mirror, PIXcel3D-Medipix3.
provenance: Instrument, material and threshold values are transcribed from procedure v4 (si/S1-procedure.md) except where a v4 value was found to be wrong: the cobalt density ceiling was 8.9, above the table bulk 8.79, contradicting v4's own rule that the bulk ceiling is the one physically meaningful bound, and is corrected here. The substrate is now taken from the substrate library; v4 carried glass at 2.65, the crystalline-quartz value. Revised 2026-09-21 by the author's decisions on the synthetic recovery benchmark (benchmark/results/FINDINGS.md; X-Ray Calc 3.9.1.950): instrument.lambda_A 1.5406 -> 1.54187, the K-alpha1 + 0.5 K-alpha2 intensity-weighted mean (ground P: 2:1 doublet, an unresolved doublet peaks at its centroid; E: the instrument file records the parallel-beam mirror with hybrid="false" and usedWavelength "K-Alpha"; Malvern Panalytical ties K-alpha1-only data to Ge crystal monochromators, and a user facility with the same optics states "graded mirror (more intense - CuKa1,2)"; the mirror datasheet itself was not seen). With 1.5406 the benchmark's period came out 0.055 A short; with 1.54187, 0.011 A. optimizer.seeds.count 3 -> 5: three seeds understated the seed std about 2.5-fold; the std is stable from five seeds on (ground E). optimizer.lock_interlayer_thickness true (ground I: the author's profile model; with a water-cooled substrate holder intermixing does not drift, deposition rates do). Kept, now ground E: reporting.model_selection.margin_in_seed_spreads 2.0 (a 5 % drift scored 8.3-13.5 seed spreads, no drift at most 0.1), optimizer.population.multilayer 5000 and optimizer.iterations 100 (500/2000 and 50 worse, more no better). Second revision 2026-09-21 (author's decisions on stages B and C of the benchmark): chi2.multilayer.theta_weight 1 -> 0. Ground E: over 20 noise realisations per cell, compared curve by curve, weight 0 beat weight 1 on the cobalt thickness and the metal sum in 80 % of realisations (rms 0.05 vs 0.13 A) and on the surface layer in 95 % (0.31 vs 0.57 A); on W/B4C it beat it on the tungsten density in 95 % (0.40 vs 0.70 g/cm3). Only the period preferred weight 1, by 0.01 A. acceptance.thresholds.chi2_max 10 -> 1.3 and acceptance.calibrated_under.chi2.theta_weight -> 0, because a chi-squared threshold means nothing outside the weighting it was calibrated under: the same converged fit of CoC4 scores 6.572 at weight 1 and 0.823 at weight 0, and of CoC5 2.836 and 0.662 (this laboratory's curves, measured 2026-09-21 on 3.9.1.950, 3 seeds, population 5000). The new value keeps the margin the old one had over the calibration curves themselves (10 / 6.572 = 1.52; 1.52 x 0.823 = 1.25, rounded to 1.3); it was not obtained by scaling 10 by the chi-squared ratio, which is curve-dependent (0.125 on CoC4, 0.233 on CoC5). The other thresholds are ratios and do not move with the weighting. Pass rates of the recomputed campaigns under this threshold, measured 2026-09-21 by replaying all 158 stored fit requests on 3.9.1.950 (analysis/recompute-2026-09-21): 37 % of fits pass at weight 0 and chi2_max 1.3 (Co/C 66 %, Ru/C 8 %), against 62 % under the study's weight 1 and chi2_max 10 (Co/C 91 %, Ru/C 33 %). The author kept 1.3 (decision 2026-09-21): the threshold follows the calibration curves rather than a target pass rate. Note that the non-transfer is not an artefact of the weighting: in UNWEIGHTED chi2 the Ru/C curves still sit about 2.3-fold above the Co/C ones (median 2.73 against 1.20), so no choice of weighting makes one threshold carry across the two material systems. Third revision 2026-09-22 (v5.0.1, draft pending the author's tag): a scale section is added, because the released engine 3.9.2.970 solves the scale inside the objective by default (author's decision 6, 2026-09-22) while v5.0 described only the anchored scale and sent no scale_solve or scale_solve_window. scale.solve true (ground C plus E: benchmark R6/R8, against a wrong anchor the solve caps the damage at its own bias, and at the correct anchor it about halves the Co density bias; on the published engine, stage E, the Co density error at the anchored scale is +0.072 +/- 0.012 with the solve against +0.166 without, benchmark/results/xrc-3.9.2.970 vs gate-5d3fb22). scale.solve_window 0.7, the author's rulings of 2026-09-22 (first "the window must be larger, I would say 50%", then "0.7 and rerun"): the engine default 0.2 clamped the solve on the real glass 260921B, which wants a ratio of 1.476 (analysis/glass-260921B-2026-09-22.md), and on the published-engine re-study in 15 of 240 stage-E, 54 of 240 stage-F and 10 of the first 199 stage-G fits, all dim or badly anchored cells. acceptance.calibrated_under gains scale_solve false: chi2_max 1.3 was fixed with the scale anchored on 3.9.1.950, a solved chi-squared is never higher than the anchored one for the same structure, so the threshold is not calibrated for the default and is to be re-derived from the re-study on the published binary. Fourth revision 2026-09-23 (v5.0.2, the author's ruling "select what is best" on the measurement below): chi2_max stays 1.3 and is now fixed under the solve. Ground E: the two calibration fits replayed on the published engine 3.9.2.970 at theta_weight 0, five seeds, with the scale anchored and solved within window 0.7 (analysis/recompute-2026-09-21/chi2max-solve-e9ad011.md): CoC4 1.039 -> 1.011 (-2.7 %), CoC5 0.986 -> 0.903 (-8.4 %), no fit clamped. The margin rule above applied to the solved chi-squared gives 1.52 x 0.823 x 0.973 = 1.22 against the anchored 1.25; at the one-decimal resolution of the threshold, and with a factor that is curve-dependent (0.97 on CoC4, 0.92 on CoC5) and measured under the campaign requests rather than this preset's conditioning, the two are the same band, so the value is kept rather than moved on a precision the calibration does not have. Provenance gap, recorded here because it cannot be closed: the calibration values 6.572 / 0.823 (CoC4) and 2.836 / 0.662 (CoC5) of the second revision have no record outside this text; the stored campaign requests of the same two fits give 1.039 (CoC4) and 0.986 (CoC5) at weight 0 on 3.9.1.950 and 3.9.2.970 alike (analysis/recompute-2026-09-21/recompute.jsonl, recompute-e9ad011-solveoff.jsonl), so the second revision's numbers were measured under a conditioning that was not written down. A fit of CoC4 and CoC5 under this preset itself would close the gap and is the ground to prefer when it exists.

C.reason: Sputtered carbon reaches 2.4, above the Henke bulk table value of 2.266; the ceiling is raised deliberately.

Co.reason: Ceiling is the bulk density. Procedure v4 used 8.9, above the table bulk value of 8.79, which contradicted its own rule that the bulk ceiling is the one physically meaningful bound; corrected in v5.

B4C.reason: Ceiling is the bulk density 2.52 from the author's record (2026-09-21), not the 2.37 the engine's Henke table reports. That table value is hand-typed in the table editor with no derivation and no provenance; CXRO's B4C entry is 2.52 and the handbook range is 2.45-2.52. Ground X (author's record) plus ground E: with the ceiling at 2.37 the recovery benchmark could not reach its own T3 truth of 2.40 - across stage C the fitted B4C density had median 2.3672 and 22 % of fits sat within 0.001 of the ceiling, while W absorbed the missing electron density at +0.483 g/cm3. Floor and start follow the default rule, 0.7 and 0.9 of bulk.

sigma_A.reason: Ground E: synthetic recovery benchmark on X-Ray Calc 3.9.1.950, 2026-09-21 (benchmark/results/FINDINGS.md, item 12): a true sigma of 7.5 A, 0.5 A from the upper bound, was recovered within 0.22 A; widening to [0.5, 12] changed nothing. Originally the author's recollection of practice, carried over from procedure v4. Start range 3-5 A: with range_seed the start plays no part in the search.

smoothing.reason: Ground E: stage D2 of the recovery benchmark, 2026-09-21 (benchmark/results/FINDINGS.md items 18-20, benchmark/analyze_d.py). Holding the bright curve's fitting range at every brightness so that only the counting noise varies, one pass is the better of the pair in 39 / 47 / 28 / 35 % of paired comparisons at plateau counts 605000 / 87000 / 17000 / 3600, and on the clean truth alone (T1, no parameter near a bound) in 30 / 48 / 22 / 30 %. It never rises above even, and the dimmest curve - where a pass was expected to pay - is among the worst, so there is no count at which to switch it on and no threshold key is offered. The period is what it damages most: on T3 one pass is never the better of the pair at any level. Procedure v4 and earlier prescribed exactly one pass, always; this replaces that. Only the engine's default window (SmoothWindow -1) was tested, so 'off' is measured against one default pass and not against a narrower one.

fitting_range.reason: Ground E: benchmark stages H2, H3 and H4, 2026-09-22 (benchmark/results/FINDINGS.md R9-R10, benchmark/analyze_h2.py), 960 fits at 10 realisations x 3 seeds on both truths. The rule - the range covers at least the first 7 orders the refined period predicts, visible or not, never past the measured end - is v5's previous end (half a spacing past the last visible order) when 7 or more are visible, and longer when fewer are. Against that previous end, pooled over both truths and six parameters: 1.00 at 7 visible (any extension there costs 1.19, T1 2.14), 0.96 at 5-6, 0.70 at 4-5, 0.84 at 3-4. Where the endpoint was swept the gain has a minimum at the seventh order (+1 1.07, +2 0.96, +3 0.70, whole curve 0.90), so it is not 'longer is better'. Seven is the count of orders this laboratory's bright curves show. It holds with point_weight on, as here, and not with it off (R9). With the moving-average window held at a fixed point count T3 keeps its gain and T1 keeps little, so on T3 the tail carries evidence about the layer split and on T1 much of the gain is the wider weighting window the longer range brings. Not tested on films (the fringe rule stands) or on designs showing more than seven orders bright, where the rule does nothing.

scale.reason: Ground C (author's decisions 2026-09-22: solve on by default; window first 50%, then 70% the same evening) plus ground E: recovery benchmark R6 and R8 (a wrong anchor maps almost linearly into the heavy-layer density, a 15% anchor error costing 0.67 g/cm3 in Co; the solve caps that at its own bias and about halves the bias at a correct anchor) and the published-engine re-study, where the engine default window 0.2 clamped the solve in 15/240 stage-E, 54/240 stage-F and 10/199 stage-G fits. The window is the factor the solved scale may move from the anchored one either way: 0.7 allows 1.7 up and 0.588 down. The real glass 260921B needs 1.476, inside with margin; a curve anchored worse than 1.7-fold still clamps, and scale_clamped true is then reported with the fit (section 4 rule 3). The solve does not remove the bias a wrong anchor leaves on Co (R8); measuring the scale from a glass tail removes it, and the solve protects the operator.
